answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit claims, then slash that stake when randomly sampled peers prove a claim false. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital and each new identity increases the amount exposed to challenge; splitting stake across aliases does not multiply voting weight. A bridge operator, grove steward, or inlet trader therefore pays a real opportunity cost for every Sybil, while honest agents recover their stake and earn fees.
